tagline: Color, squash, build, and find a match.
bigIdea: One dinosaur, many ways to notice.

dinosaur.name: Stegosaurus
dinosaur.feature: Stegosaurus had back plates and tail spikes.

letter.hint: Say /s/, not the letter name. Let {{them}} listen or echo.

number.focus: Match 3, then 4; stop at the amount requested.
number.parentTip: Match three, then four. Keep numeral strips aside while matching; five is for another willing turn.

books.title: How Do Dinosaurs Say Good Night?
books.author: Jane Yolen; art: Mark Teague

books.title: Ten Little Dinosaurs
books.author: Mike Brownlow; art: Simon Rickerty
books.note: Count a few; no need to reach ten.

songs: We Are the Dinosaurs — Laurie Berkner. March or sway.
Five Enormous Dinosaurs — traditional. Stomp and count a few.
Stomp Like a Dinosaur — Super Simple. Hear /s/ in “stomp.”
materials: 8 magnet tiles (4 each of 2 colors), cloth
parentNote: Stay and play for 2–10 minutes. Choose one route; stop on pushback. Books and songs are choices, not a checklist.

days.title: Hello, Stegosaurus!
days.invitation: Want to color Stegosaurus, or roll a dough loop for it?
days.decision: Which spoken word starts with /s/: sun or cup?
days.harder: If that sound game is easy, try a fresh spoken pair: ball or sock.
days.what: Want to color Stegosaurus, or roll a dough loop for it? Share the dinosaur strip as you play. Let {{them}} color or join the ends of a dough snake. A free crayon circle on scrap is welcome too. For a sound turn, say “sun” and “cup” naturally; ask which starts with /s/. If the words or game are new, show one together first. Point to S and model /s/; an echo is welcome. If {{they}} want{{s}} a repeat, reverse the spoken word order.
days.why: A familiar spoken word gives the new sound somewhere to belong.

days.title: Match the eggs
days.invitation: Want to make dough eggs, or build their pen with magnet tiles?
days.decision: Which card has the same number of eggs as the target?
days.harder: Empty the pen, gather eight dough eggs outside it, and invite five if four was easy.
days.exitCheck: When you asked for three or four eggs, how many did {{they}} put in?
days.what: Want to make dough eggs, or build their pen with magnet tiles? While {{they}} make{{s}} dough eggs, join four tiles into a pen; if {{they}} build{{s}} the pen, make the eggs. Then put a three-egg card above two choices (three and four); set the spare card aside. Let {{them}} find the same amount. Shuffle choices and switch the target to four when {{they}} want{{s}} another go. Fill the pen with the matching number; tile count does not matter.
days.why: Different arrangements keep the choice about quantity, not position.

Stop on pushback.
days.needs: Page, card, scissors, dough for eight eggs, washable mat, eight magnet tiles; parent present.

days.title: Find Stegosaurus’s shadow
days.invitation: Want to find Stegosaurus’s shadow, or hide its picture for me?
days.decision: Which of the three dinosaur shadows belongs to Stegosaurus?
days.harder: Hide the picture and invite its name and food while {{they}} look{{s}} at the shadow.
days.exitCheck: What did {{they}} call Stegosaurus or remember about its food?
days.what: Want to find Stegosaurus’s shadow, or hide its picture for me? Name Stegosaurus while {{they}} handle{{s}} the picture. Let {{them}} point to its shadow or park the picture below it; it need not fit exactly. Talk about plates and spikes afterward; share that it ate plants. If {{they}} choose{{s}} hiding, close your eyes while {{they}} cover{{s}} the picture; then you find it. Swap roles if {{they}} want{{s}} a turn finding.
days.why: Comparing three dinosaur shapes makes the plates and horns useful clues.

days.title: What comes next?
days.invitation: Want to build a tile trail, or choose the next picture?
days.decision: Which picture continues the leaf–egg pattern?
days.harder: After {{their}} first tile choice, offer one more place, with both colors available again.
days.exitCheck: What did {{they}} choose to come next?
days.what: Want to build a tile trail, or choose the next picture? Show red–blue–red–blue and add red together. Take it all apart. Then lay blue–red–blue–red; offer one tile of each color for the next place. Or name the printed row together, leaving its blank for {{name}}. Keep both picture choices available; {{they}} can point or park a card below the blank. One route is enough.
days.why: The objects change, but the repeating relationship stays the same.
days.cardBlurb: Four red and four blue magnet tiles (any two colors work). Cut the two picture choices; keep the row whole. Want to build a tile trail, or choose the next picture? Show red–blue–red–blue and add red together. Take it all apart. Then lay blue–red–blue–red; offer one tile of each color for the next place. Or name the printed row together, leaving its blank for {{name}}. Keep both picture choices available; {{they}} can point or park a card below the blank. One route is enough. Stop on pushback.
days.needs: Page, card, scissors, eight magnet tiles (four each of two colors); parent present.

days.title: A book for Stegosaurus
days.invitation: Want to turn the pages while I read, or make a dough resting place first?
days.decision: Which picture word starts with /s/: ball or sock?
days.harder: Cover the pictures and invite the sound for S, if {{they}} want{{s}} another turn.
days.exitCheck: Did {{they}} make a crayon circle with the ends meeting?
days.what: Want to turn the pages while I read, or make a dough resting place first? Read the captions as {{they}} turn{{s}} pages; {{they}} {{is}} not expected to read them. Talk about the dinosaur eating plants. Name “ball” and “sock” naturally before asking which starts with /s/. Show S and model the sound. On the last page, {{they}} can join a dough snake into a resting loop, or make {{their}} own crayon circle on scrap. No need to do every part. If {{they}} want{{s}} a repeat, reverse the spoken word order.
days.why: Familiar sounds return in a short book {{they}} can hold and help tell.
